correctness.rationale: The top and bottom vertex Eulerian equations imply a cyclic constant flux j=0,1,2,3. At j=0,3 all bits are forced and triangles cannot flip. At j=1 the exhaustive local edge-state trichotomy has only one illegal cyclic transition Y→Z, and a two-bit coding gives precisely independent sets of C_{2n}, reconstructing every vertical bit uniquely. The two belt triangles toggle exactly the first/second cyclic bits, so the full graph is Lucas_{2n}; global reversal gives sector j=2. Intrinsic independent-set arguments prove distances, median property, unique diametral pair, and vertex/edge totals. Independently coded finite graph verifiers confirm n=3..9 and raw-orientation enumeration n=3..8; bounded checks are supplementary.

originality.rationale: The precise new claim is an edge-preserving bijection between the n-antiprism triangular-belt-face reversal graph of balanced orientations and two isolated states plus two Lucas cubes, with flux classification. The closest primary work proves general planar Eulerian-orientation lattices (Felsner 2004) and face-reversal-chain behavior using all eligible faces (Creed 2007), or analyzes Lucas cubes intrinsically (Munarini et al. 2001; Codara and D'Antona 2014). None of the inspected full texts identifies this graph or states the cap-excluded flux-sector isomorphism. Published research-record and scholarly keyword searches located related but mathematically different constructions. Novelty remains best-knowledge, not a uniqueness certificate.

value.rationale: The exact result classifies every state and every local move for a natural infinite family of four-regular planar graphs, exposing an unexpected conserved flux, exactly two immobile states and two median/isometric hypercube components. It clarifies the sharp effect of excluding cap faces on general planar face-flip connectivity and gives constructive shortest paths. The significant object and move constraints are motivated by physical Eulerian-flow reversals, not an arbitrary numerical slice; old Lucas cube properties are credited.
